chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Hassan al-Jammal, who said:

I carried Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from Medina to Mecca. So when we arrived at Masjid al-Ghadir, he looked to the left side of the mosque and said: 'That is the place where the foot of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) set, where he said: 'For whomever I am his Mawla, Ali is his Mawla.'
Then he looked to the other side and said: 'That is the place of the tents of So-and-so, and So-and-so, and Salim, the Mawla of Abu Hudhayfa, and Abu Ubaydah al-Jarrah.'
So when they saw him raising his hands, some of them said to others: 'Look at his eyes; they are rolling as if they were the eyes of a madman.'

So Jibreel (peace be upon him) descended with this Verse: 'And those who disbelieve would almost smite you with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: He is mad. And it is naught but a Reminder to the Worlds.'

key_terms.الذِّكْرَ: The Reminder, referring to the Quran or the divine message
key_terms.رَافِعاً يَدَيْهِ: Raising his hands, a gesture of the Prophet during proclamation or prayer
key_terms.فُسْطَاطُ: Tent or dwelling of a companion
key_terms.لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ: They would almost cause you to slip/fall, referring to the piercing gaze of disbelievers
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْغَدِيرِ: Masjid al-Ghadir, the mosque/location in Khumm where the declaration of Wilayah took place
key_terms.مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلَاهُ: The famous phrase 'For whomever I am his Mawla', indicating authority and leadership

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Masjid al-Ghadir in relation to the Prophet's declaration of Imam Ali's Wilayah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the geographical sanctity of Ghadir Khumm, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the precise spot of the Prophet’s declaration of Wilayah and the location of his companions' tents. It links the Prophet’s intense, visionary gaze during the announcement to the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Qalam, illustrating how the Quraysh’s accusation of madness was a reaction to the divine weight of the message. This connection underscores the continuity of prophetic authority and the specific historical context of the Ghadir event within Shia exegetical tradition.
